description: Neuronit is a team of programmers, AI developers, researchers, and technology enthusiasts from Tajikistan, united by curiosity about space and innovation. We build practical digital products using software, artificial intelligence, data analysis, and visualization.
summary: "Artifacts of Silence" is an immersive web-based digital archive developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. While public attention focuses exclusively on active missions, dozens of historic landers, rovers, and probes sit silently across the Moon, Mars, and deep space after completing their heroic missions. Our project addresses the challenge by giving these "forgotten pioneers" a voice. It combines verified open data from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) with powerful first-person emotional storytelling, allowing users to explore historic relics through interactive world filtering, technical mission dossiers, and a time-lapse space dust slider. Built to inspire future engineers and preserve planetary heritage, the project features a futuristic NASA control room UI and honors local hackathon organizers at American Space Dushanbe.
details:
🚀 WHAT IT DOES

"Artifacts of Silence" is an interactive web platform that catalogues discarded NASA equipment on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space, transforming cold technical telemetry into a living, breathing historical archive.

  • World Filtering: Seamlessly filter relics across celestial bodies: [The Moon], [Mars], and [Deep Space / Orbit].
  • Voice of the Machine: Emotional first-person monologues written from the perspective of the machines, turning titanium and solar panels into touching historical testaments.
  • Technical Dossiers: Direct integration of official NASA NSSDCA telemetry data, COSPAR IDs, exact landing coordinates, and preserved scientific payloads.
  • Time-Lapse & Visuals: Interactive space dust accumulation slider (1969–2026) paired with historical image galleries and a welcome tribute modal honoring American Space Dushanbe.

🛰️ BUILT ON REAL NASA DATA & ARCHIVES

  • NASA NSSDCA Master Catalogs: Comprehensive tracking of mission parameters, landing chronology, and scientific instrument records.
  • NASA Image and Video Library & JPL Photojournal: High-resolution archival imagery, surface panoramas, and self-portraits (e.g., Apollo 11 Eagle, Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, and Dawn).
  • Curated Relics: Full dossiers on 8 legendary space milestones, including Apollo Lunar Modules, rovers (Spirit, Opportunity, Sojourner), landers (Viking 1 & 2, InSight, Phoenix), and deep space probes (Dawn, Kepler).

🎯 BENEFITS AND IMPACT

The project bridges the gap between cold scientific data and human empathy. Its intended impact is to educate students, inspire the public, and preserve the historical legacy of space exploration. It is free, runs in any desktop or mobile browser, needs no installation, and engages young developers and students across Tajikistan and globally.

🛠️ HOW WE BUILT IT

  • Frontend Stack: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, Alpine.js, and Three.js (WebGL) for high-performance responsive rendering.
  • Deployment: Deployed seamlessly via GitHub Pages.
  • Source Code: Open-source project repository maintained by Team Neuronit.

🤖 USE OF SI AND CREDITS

Code structure, research data gathering, and content refinement were assisted by AI/SI tools (Antigravity & ChatGPT) under the team's direct vision, editorial review, and curation. No NASA logos or branding were used. Artifacts of Silence is an educational digital archive and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
